title: a foreign property read reached through an index signature needs an annotated adapter exactly as a declared one does
notes:
09-foreign-calls/foreign-property-read-needs-an-adapter pins the read of a property some declaration spells. This pins the read of one that none does: `keyed.width` resolves through a `Record<string, number>` index signature, so a rule that walks a merged property's declarations finds an empty list. An empty list of declarations is not evidence of a trust claim, and treating it as one is a fail-open — the same shape as `@throws {never}` matched per symbol, one level down. FILED HONESTLY AGAINST CURRENT BEHAVIOUR: at the time this case was written the fork accepted the program, compiled it with zero diagnostics, ran it and exited 0 printing `3`, and the xfail said so. HISTORY: the fix that was in flight landed on 2026-08-26. The prediction in this note was that the case would then score XPASS; it did not, and the reason is worth keeping. The lane closed the fail-open by deleting the fork's second gate — the one that walked the MEMBER's declarations — so the property rule now asks the receiver's provenance alone, exactly as its own comment had always claimed and as the reference does. That is the whole of what this case's VIBE1506 pins, and the fork now reports it at 4:17. What the fork still does not do is charge Panic to the enclosing row, so it omits the VIBE1101, and that is a different rule with its own standing marker. The outcome was therefore a NARROWED xfail rather than a retirement: the marker survives, the direction column changed from FAIL-OPEN to fail-closed, and the sentence in the marker that described the fail-open had to be rewritten because it had become false in the same commit that made it obsolete. Its deliberate pair is 09-foreign-calls/a-foreign-index-signature-read-through-an-element-access-needs-an-adapter, the same read spelled `keyed["width"]`, which is what shows the rule follows the receiver rather than the spelling. RENAMED 2026-08-28, from `a-foreign-index-signature-read-is-refused-on-one-backend-only`. The old name described the state the case was FILED in and had been false since 2026-08-26: the READ is refused on both backends, and only the row charge is one-sided, so a name whose whole claim was "one backend only" said the opposite of what the case now pins. The name it carries instead states its subject — a foreign index-signature read reached through a PROPERTY ACCESS needs an adapter — and pairs by construction with its deliberate sibling `a-foreign-index-signature-read-through-an-element-access-needs-an-adapter`, the same read spelled `keyed["width"]`, which is what shows the rule follows the receiver rather than the spelling. The rename was previously declined because the identity was cited from three documents and a dangling citation buys one adjective at the cost of three references. That objection is answered rather than overruled: every citation was found and updated in the same change — conformance/README.md (three), conformance/COVERAGE.md (six), poc/src/language/README.md, the sibling case's own notes, and two the earlier count had missed, compiler/fork_collection_ownership_test.go and compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt. RE-MEASURED at the rename rather than assumed: the reference reports [VIBE1101@3:1, VIBE1506@4:17] and the fork reports [VIBE1506@4:17], identical to the sibling's split, which is the standing row-charge gap and not this case's subject. KEEP THIS CASE: it is still the only row that would notice the deleted second gate — the one that walked the MEMBER's declarations and read an index signature's empty declaration list as nothing to object to — coming back.

2026-09-07 retirement: measured as XPASS in the full native-only corpus run. The native boundary reporter now charges Panic to the enclosing row before inference, so both profiles report the complete authored diagnostic list, including VIBE1101. No source, required code, position or message assertion was removed.
